name: Team Roster
description: The two sides: which entities are on which team, what position each plays, and which AI role fills the empty slots. It extends social.party_system's grouping semantics to adversarial, symmetric groups with a headcount rule — a party cooperates, a roster competes, and reusing the grouping plumbing is why this component is small. Positions are data (name, zone, responsibilities) read by both utility.behavior_fsm-driven teammates and world.goal_zone's attribution, so 'goalkeeper' means the same thing to the AI and the scoreboard. Substitutions and mid-match balancing are roster mutations with events, because a silently swapped team breaks every downstream attribution and every spectator's mental model at once.

inputs.name: teamCount
inputs.description: Sides in the match. Two is the sport; three-plus is a supported variant for arena modes, kept as an input so the roster math never hardcodes a binary.

inputs.name: playersPerTeam
inputs.description: Headcount per side. The number defines the sport more than the ball does — 5 is small-sided and readable, 11 needs a minimap, and both run on this same descriptor.

inputs.name: positions
inputs.description: Named roles with zone data attached at the match level. Assignment prefers filling positions in order, because a team of five forwards is a highlight reel for exactly one side.

inputs.name: fillWithAI
inputs.description: Whether empty slots get behavior-driven teammates. The AI role receives the position's zone and responsibilities verbatim — an AI left back and a human left back should be interchangeable to every system but the input one.

inputs.name: allowSubstitutions
inputs.description: Whether bench swaps are legal mid-match. Substitutions emit events rather than mutating quietly, since a swap mid-play changes who the referee and the scoreboard think anyone is.

outputs.name: rosterSizes
outputs.description: Live headcount per team, humans and AI together. Balance checks and forfeit rules read this; nobody maintains a shadow count.

outputs.name: teamsFull
outputs.description: True when every side meets playersPerTeam. Match-start gates read this rather than re-deriving fullness from the roster.
